The exclusive=true/false semantics, execution lanes → "couloirs d'exécution", the credential-protection caveat and the "no shared cluster-wide quantum access" limitation all match the English. editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. examples.translation: Nouveau dans l'informatique quantique ? ... Déjà familier avec Qiskit ?

editor_note: The translation is faithful and does not mislead. The core terms are correct and used consistently: produit scalaire, conjugué transposé, mesure projective, mesure dans la base standard, matrice par blocs and procédé de Gram–Schmidt. A few terminology calques should still be fixed. In [45], "conjugue linéaire" is an odd calque and does not match [40]'s own heading, "linéarité conjuguée"; "antilinéaire" or "linéaire conjugué" is standard. In [33], the property "positive definiteness" is named with an adjective ("appelée définie positive") instead of a noun such as "caractère défini positif". In [94], "Par précaution" misreads "As a word of caution", and in [146] "qu'on choisit d'être |0⟩" is a calque of the English.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. That includes the harder parts: the dimension proof (2^{n-r}), the three error-detection cases, the Steane distance-3 argument and the correction bound of (d-1)/2. The terms are consistent too (générateurs stabilisateurs, espace de code, erreurs de déphasage, poids minimal) and the tu register holds. A few surface slips remain. [138] has the typo "anti-communterait". [22] and [139] contain the English calques "ce qui est équivalent à … n'étant pas contenu" and "C'est donc le cas que". editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through: the no-signalling argument in [42], the separable/entangled definitions in [25]-[27] and the partial-trace passages match the English, and the informal "tu" register holds. A few phrases are calqued from English and a native editor would change them. "uniquement déterminée" [49] should be "déterminée de manière unique", because "uniquement" reads as "only". examples.source: for a uniquely determined collection of vectors
examples.translation: pour une collection de vecteurs … uniquement déterminée

examples.source: have unit trace
examples.translation: ont une trace unitaire
examples.suggested: sont de trace 1 (ou : ont une trace égale à 1)

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The SQD/SKQD steps, the convergence conditions (sparse ground state, energy gap "pas trop faible") and the Slurm partition details all match the source, and "tu" is used consistently. The problems are in wording. "sparse" is left in English as an adjective ("sous-espace sparse", "opérateurs de Pauli sont sparse", "non sparse") where a French writer would use "creux" or "parcimonieux". "états de base computationnels" is a calque of "computational basis states"; the usual French is "états de la base de calcul". A few sentences read as translationese, such as "conduira l'état de plus en plus proche", "plus compactement exprimables" and "fonctionnalités puissantes". Entry [31] also drops the "at all" nuance, and entry [61] attaches "complexes" to the impurities instead of the models.

examples.source: well-approximated by a sparse subspace
examples.translation: bien approximé par un sous-espace sparse
examples.suggested: bien approché par un sous-espace creux (ou parcimonieux)
examples.why: English adjective left unadapted in French prose; 'creux'/'parcimonieux' is the usual French term. The same issue appears in [26], [59] and [64].

examples.source: project the ansatz onto computational basis states
examples.translation: projeter rapidement l'ansatz sur des états de base computationnels
examples.suggested: projeter rapidement l'ansatz sur des états de la base de calcul
examples.why: 'computationnels' is a calque; French QC texts say 'base de calcul'.

examples.source: The algorithm itself will then drive the state closer and closer to the ground state
examples.translation: L'algorithme lui-même conduira ensuite l'état de plus en plus proche de l'état fondamental
examples.suggested: L'algorithme lui-même rapprochera ensuite progressivement l'état de l'état fondamental
examples.why: The structure 'conduire X proche de' is calqued from English and is not idiomatic French.

examples.source: If these are sampled at all, even if their overlap with our ansatz is small

examples.suggested: Pour peu qu'elles soient échantillonnées ne serait-ce qu'une fois, même si leur chevauchement avec notre ansatz est faible

examples.translation: modèles d'Anderson à 4 impuretés complexes

examples.source: Utilities

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the SQD/VQE contrast, the 70% badge threshold and the quiz-attempt limit, and the "tu" register holds. examples.source: Lesson 1: Variational quantum eigensolver

examples.source: what factors determine the scaling of approaches

examples.translation: Adapter un exemple de problème à leur propre problème d'intérêt.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The BB84 steps, the no-cloning argument, the 14% and 23% mismatch figures and the caveats are all translated faithfully, and nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are wording. "One-time pad" is rendered literally as "bloc-notes à usage unique" where French cryptography says "masque jetable". Eavesdropping is rendered three ways ("espionnage", "écoute", "écoute clandestine"), and "notebook" appears both as "notebook" [111] and as "carnets" [134]. There are also some calques: "le déchiffrer est totalement désespéré" [45], "Pour le dire avec euphémisme" [28], "opération unitaire (quantique mécanique)" [95] and "aucune base sur laquelle fonder" [91], which puns awkwardly on quantum bases. The last entry [166] slips into "vous" (Supposez/considérez/Discutez) and spells "Eve" instead of "Ève".

examples.source: This is called a “one-time pad”.

examples.why: The standard French cryptography term is 'masque jetable'. The literal rendering is recognizable but not what a French learner will find in the literature.

examples.suggested: il n'existe pas d'opération unitaire (relevant de la mécanique quantique)

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the last 40%. The uncertainty relations, the eigenstate reasoning in [95]-[107] and the noise caveat in [114] all match the source, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are calques. The Check-your-understanding questions use ungrammatical English-shaped syntax: "Quels états t'attendrais-tu à avoir une incertitude nulle dans X ?" and the redundant "ensemble en tant qu'ensemble". "Où les résultats retournent…" in [100] is not a sentence. "Incertitude dans X" (entries [90]-[106]) should be "incertitude sur X", as the file itself writes in [11]. Also, "valeur d'espérance" is a calque; French physics texts say "valeur moyenne", which should replace it throughout the file. Small slips: "environ ~30 secondes" in [7] is redundant, "very slightly" became plain "légèrement" in [114], and [116] turns an instruction into a question.

examples.source: (a) What states would you expect to have zero uncertainty in $X$?
examples.translation: (a) Quels états t'attendrais-tu à avoir une incertitude nulle dans $X$ ?
examples.suggested: (a) Pour quels états t'attendrais-tu à une incertitude nulle sur $X$ ?
examples.why: Calqued syntax that is ungrammatical in French, and 'dans X' should be 'sur X' as in [11]. [91] has the same problem.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the measurement-versus-operator argument, the 3/5 and 2/5 probabilities and the true/false questions, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The main problem is that "angular momentum" is split. It is "moment cinétique" in [11]-[52] and switches to "moment angulaire" from [92] onward. "Collapse" is also split, as "collapse" in [106] and [134] but "s'effondre" in [158], and the repeated step-1 heading changes from "Convertir" [68] to "Transformer" [93]. examples.source: an angle at which an angular momentum vector would emerge from the oven
examples.translation: l'angle selon lequel un vecteur de moment angulaire émergerait du four
examples.suggested: l'angle selon lequel un vecteur de moment cinétique sortirait du four

examples.suggested: pour expliquer le comportement quantique de l'atome

examples.suggested: tu as un aimant de taille atomique qui ne peut dissiper aucune énergie

examples.translation: une particule qui s'effondre dans un état définitivement le long de +x

examples.suggested: Déterminer $x$ analytiquement

examples.source: where $x$ are our coefficients of interest
examples.translation: où $x$ sont nos coefficients d'intérêt
examples.suggested: où $x$ désigne les coefficients recherchés

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The budget logic, truncation-error bound, slice counts (7 slices, 6 of 8 groups, 3 more slices) and the qubit-wise commuting stop condition all match the English, and "tu" is used throughout. examples.translation: le nombre de termes dans l'opérateur tendra généralement à approcher $4^N$ rapidement

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The ~16 mH and 1.6 mH chemical-accuracy figures, the caveat that the samples are pure noise, the zig-zag/heavy-hex layout and the Job execution mode all come through intact, and the "tu" register is consistent. examples.source: occupy the first five orbitals with high probability
examples.translation: occupent les cinq premières orbitales avec une haute probabilité
examples.suggested: occupent les cinq premières orbitales avec une forte probabilité

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The measurement-0/1 correction logic, the DD caveat and the conclusions about depth and duration all match the English, but several terms and register choices need an editor. "Classical feedforward" is "feedforward classique" everywhere except [72], which switches to "rétroaction classique". "Rétroaction" means feedback, so the file both drifts and names the wrong concept. "Effectively implemented" is calqued as "effectivement implémentée" in [30] and [32], and in French that reads as "indeed implemented". "Kicked Ising" becomes "Ising perturbé" in [0], [1] and [5], which suggests a small perturbation rather than a periodic kick ("pulsé" or "à impulsions" is the usual term). The register slips into vous in [4] ("Votre temps"), [29] and [30] ("Notez que"), while [63] uses "Note que".

examples.why: Everywhere else the file uses 'feedforward classique' and 'en milieu de circuit'. 'Rétroaction' means feedback, a different concept.

examples.translation: l'interaction ZZ est effectivement implémentée en utilisant des qubits ancillaires
examples.suggested: l'interaction ZZ est implémentée de manière effective à l'aide de qubits ancillaires
examples.why: French 'effectivement' means 'indeed', not 'in effect', so it drops the idea that this is an equivalent implementation.

examples.suggested: Simulation d'un hamiltonien d'Ising pulsé avec des circuits dynamiques

examples.suggested: Note que le réseau en nid d'abeilles que nous voulons simuler

editor_note: The meaning matches the English throughout. I found no inverted conditions and no dropped caveats: the barren-plateau caveat in [56] and the "upper bound" claims in [18] and [67] are kept. The problems are word choices. "expectation value" becomes the calque "valeur d'expectation" instead of "valeur moyenne" or "valeur espérée". "spanned by" becomes "délimité par", but the linear-algebra term is "engendré par". "intractable" becomes "insoluble", which suggests the problem cannot be solved at all rather than that it is too costly to compute. A few phrases are stiff: "l'un des optimiseurs très préférés", "le matériel suivant" for "material", and "overhead de mesure".

examples.source: measuring the expectation value
examples.translation: en mesurant la valeur d'expectation
examples.suggested: en mesurant la valeur moyenne (ou valeur espérée)
examples.why: 'valeur d'expectation' is an anglicism. French quantum texts use 'valeur moyenne' or 'valeur espérée'.

examples.suggested: sur le sous-espace engendré par ces échantillons
